mechanism: TrisWeb monitors EURUSD–GBPUSD–EURJPY simultaneously and lays pending buy/sell-stop grids sized per-symbol (calm majors ~40/60 pts; volatile JPY crosses ~50/80) to capture fleeting triangular/synthetic-rate imbalances rather than predicting direction; OnTick counts orders/profits across the three legs and closes the whole web when total profit (incl. swap+commission) exceeds target.
data_needed: Live Bid/Ask for three related FX pairs; per-symbol Step01/Step02; Deviation; work-time window; account balance for AutoLot.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURJPY (and analogous triangles); tick-driven MT5; multi-year live including pandemic vol.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional synthetic-parity imbalance sensor with per-leg volatility-scaled spacing—MIS can flag relative-value dislocation regimes without single-symbol forecasts.
quote: it mathematically calculates potential imbalances between three related currency pairs and places a grid of orders ready to catch these imbalances when they arise.

mechanism: IsWorkTime/CheckNewDayAndWorkTime circadian gate: EA only places/refreshes grids inside configured hours and deletes stale pending orders at each new workday open, avoiding overnight wide-spread/unnatural moves.
data_needed: Local time Start/End hour-minute; IsNewDayReset flag; DeleteAllOrders on day rollover.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX triangle; session-clock on broker/local time.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit session liquidity/spread regime gate MIS can reuse to silence other sensors when overnight microstructure is unreliable.
quote: There are times when it is best to step aside — the overnight session, with its wide spreads and unnatural movements, often brings more problems than opportunities.

mechanism: DUET Temporal Clustering Module (TCM): parallel MoE encoders (conv 2-layer SoftPlus experts) on time segments; Noisy Gating projects mean/variance per expert, Top-K logits (+train-time noise, Softplus std) SoftMax-weighted so only k most probable latent temporal distributions process each segment—adapts to economic-cycle/volatility phases.
data_needed: Multivariate HistoryBars×BarDescr; experts (e.g. 16) and top_k (e.g. 4); OpenCL TopKgates/TopKgatesGrad; train vs infer noise switch.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multivariate financial TS; EURUSD M1 in final-part tests.
why_new_for_mis: Latent temporal-cluster gate is a direct market-phase/regime sensor: which expert mix is active signals regime identity without hand-labeled regimes.
quote: Temporal clustering (TCM) groups data based on similar characteristics and allows models to adapt to changes over time. In financial market analysis, this makes it possible to account for different phases of economic cycles.

mechanism: Channel Clustering Module: FFT of each channel → amplitude-spectrum vector distances (simplified vs Mahalanobis) → normalize to [0,1] → inverse-distance channel mask; Fusion multiplies temporal Self-Attention scores by CCM mask before SoftMax; two stacked CNeuronDUET blocks use Attraos-style phase-space steps 5 and 15 on M1 (5-/15-min embeddings) then Actor+direction probability.
data_needed: Transposed multivariate series; FFT power-of-two pad; MaskByDistance OpenCL; DUET experts/top_k; EURUSD M1 HistoryBars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; train 2024 (batch 1 then 60); test Jan–Feb 2025 (53 trades, PF 2.44).
why_new_for_mis: Frequency-domain cross-channel correlation mask + dual phase-lag DUET stack gives MIS a joint regime/cross-asset dependency sensor that adapts when crisis correlations shift.
quote: CCM performs channel clustering using the frequency characteristics of signals.... Analyzing the distances between amplitude vectors of the channels' frequency characteristics makes it possible to identify correlated signals and eliminate noise phenomena.

mechanism: Per FX pair: swap_ratio=max(|swap_long|,|swap_short|)/spread; direction prefers higher swap side; combined_score = w_swap·norm(avg_swap) + w_return·norm(levered market return) − w_vol·norm(levered volatility); Markowitz/SLSQP maximizes Sharpe of (market+swap) returns under Σ|w_i|S_i>0 and covariance hedging.
data_needed: MT5 symbol_info swap_long/short, spread, point; D1 history from 2015; config swap_weight/return_weight/volatility_weight; leverage.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi FX (e.g. GBPAUD, EURNZD, EURCAD, AUDNZD, GBPJPY, USDJPY, CHFJPY, EURJPY); D1 2015–2025.
why_new_for_mis: Integrates carry (swap), cost (spread), and vol into one pair-attractiveness sensor plus correlation-aware portfolio state—MIS can track carry-regime and stress-stable funding flow.
quote: True magic happens at the intersection of three dimensions: market return, swaps, and volatility.... Positive swaps ensure a stable daily flow of funds.

mechanism: AdaptiveQ Enhanced: 531,441-hash market states from M15/H1/H4 (MA diffs, RSI, Stoch, momentum, MA-above flags) per 7 majors; DetermineActionNash adjusts each symbol’s Q-action scores by corr×otherScore×0.05 only when |corr|>0.3; causal Q updates also bleed reward to correlated symbols (|corr|>0.2); opportunity-cost adaptive learning rate when chosen action lost but alternative would have won.
data_needed: Seven FX symbols; correlationMatrix; multi-TF MA/RSI/Stoch caches; Q-matrix[state][6 actions][symbol]; corr thresholds 0.3/0.2.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Seven major FX pairs; M15, H1, H4 simultaneous; bar-periodic Q save.
why_new_for_mis: Correlation-thresholded Nash cross-pair action coupling is a multi-asset regime/interaction sensor MIS can use when pairwise dependence exceeds noise.
quote: A correlation is taken into account only if its absolute value exceeds 0.3. This allows you to filter out the "noise" and focus on the really significant relationships between currency pairs.

mechanism: DADA Adaptive Bottlenecks: pool of mini-autoencoders with different latent sizes; noisy router selects top-k compression routes per patch so meaningful signal keeps detail while noisy segments compress harder; dual adversarial decoders (normal reconstruction vs anomaly divergence); train with artificial noise anomalies; deploy uses normal decoder only—large reconstruction error ⇒ anomaly.
data_needed: Patched/masked multivariate TS; bottlenecks[] latent widths; Top-K router; normal+anomaly decoder paths; generative noise for anomaly examples.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: General TS anomaly setting; trading stack EURUSD M1 in final part.
why_new_for_mis: Context-dependent compression + reconstruction-error anomaly score is a market-state change/anomaly sensor that adapts bottleneck tightness to local structure instead of fixed PCA rank.
quote: Instead of a fixed compression level, it employs multiple options and selects the most suitable one for each case.... If reconstruction is accompanied by significant errors, this indicates a potential anomaly.

mechanism: MQL5 DADA stack: batch-norm → 20% Dropout mask → transpose → two conv patch encoders → CNeuronAdaBN (15 autoencoders latent 8…120, Top-K=3) → conv decoder + RevIN; Actor concatenates account state with AdaBN latent; Probability head SoftMax on same latent for next-bar direction; reconstruction vs latent multitask training.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr EURUSD M1; Segments; EmbeddingSize; AdaBN bottlenecks×15 top_k=3; account vector; NForecast targets.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; train 2024 random runs; test Jan–Feb 2025 (57 trades, PF 1.53).
why_new_for_mis: Operational adaptive-bottleneck latent is a reusable MIS anomaly/regime embedding that jointly feeds policy and direction probability from reconstruction-trained state.
quote: Unlike traditional algorithms that require retraining when market conditions change, DADA can automatically adjust its parameters.... The ability to adapt dynamically allows the model to perform effectively across a wide range of market scenarios, from stable trends to sudden spikes in volatility.

mechanism: CATCH Forward Module: normalize → FFT → split spectrum into L patches of size P step S on real+imag → project to latent; Channel Fusion Module uses Mask Generator (Bernoulli on probabilistic D) + Channel-Masked Transformer attention within each frequency band; TFRM iFFT reconstructs series; anomalies = reconstruction error. Distinguishes point anomalies (vol spikes/HF) vs subsequence anomalies (correlation/trend shifts in LF).
data_needed: Multivariate TS; FFT complex spectrum; patch P/S; MG matrices D→mask M; ClusteringLoss; iFFT residual error.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multivariate market instruments (prices, volumes); EURUSD M1 in final-part tests.
why_new_for_mis: Band-specific frequency patching separates short-term vol anomalies from slow regime/correlation breaks—MIS can sense change type by which frequency patches fail reconstruction.
quote: short-term volatility spikes affect high-frequency components, while broader trend changes appear in low-frequency bands.... Subsequence anomalies are more subtle — they appear normal at first glance but deviate from established market patterns.

mechanism: CNeuronCATCH: transpose → FFT (pad to 2^n) → complex conv frequency patching/embedding → two CNeuronComplexMVMHMaskAttention layers (masked attention only across same-frequency patches of different univariate channels; optional pairwise segment merge) → linear heads → iFFT + residual → transpose; Encoder→Actor+direction models; patch window=8 step=1.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr; complex float2 OpenCL kernels; mask sigmoid init 0.5; window_key/heads; EURUSD M1 dataset.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; train 2024; test Jan–Mar 2025 (68 trades, ~47% wins, PF 1.72).
why_new_for_mis: Complex-domain same-band cross-channel masked attention is a concrete MIS sensor for latent inter-instrument coupling per frequency scale, scored by reconstruction residual.
quote: the CATCH framework applies attention only within individual patches corresponding to the same frequency segment but belonging to different univariate sequences.... independently identify relationships within different univariate sequences across frequency bands—separately capturing long-term trends and short-term dynamics.

mechanism: For trending assets, label only one direction (buy or sell) with random horizon; features = rolling std over windows {5,35,…,275} only (non-symmetric vol); meta_learner / multi-head bootstrap meta_learners mark chronologically bad samples via CV/bootstrap misclassification books → meta_labels gate trading; final CatBoost+ONNX one-direction EA.
data_needed: OHLC close series; markup/stop/take; direction flag; periods list; StratifiedKFold or models_number bootstrap heads; bad_samples_fraction.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; train 2020–2024; forward 2024–early 2025; buy preferred on uptrend gold.
why_new_for_mis: Trend-regime-aware unidirectional labeling plus vol-only features and bad-sample meta-gating gives MIS a clean long-bias/short-bias regime filter when bidirectional class geometry fails.
quote: In situations where an asset has a clearly defined unidirectional trend, trading systems that imply buys and sells may be too risky.... Features are optimized for only one type of patterns (for example, trend continuation).

mechanism: Train small MLP on normalized price history to predict a dynamic attractor level; Oscillator=(CurrentPrice/Attractor−1)×100 as overbought/oversold vs learned mean-reversion magnet; tanh activation; optional MA smoothing of oscillator; entries when oscillator exits dynamic bands and turns back.
data_needed: Close history TrainBars; InputNeurons lookback; HiddenNeurons; LearningRate; PredictionPeriod; optional SmoothingPeriod.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart symbol/TF (scalp minutes to positional days via PredictionPeriod); NeuralAttractor_v2.mq5 indicator.
why_new_for_mis: Learned dynamic equilibrium level (vs static SMA) yields an adaptive overextension regime sensor MIS can use for mean-reversion stress without fixed window averages.
quote: we compare the current price with the predicted attractor and express deviation as a percentage.... If the oscillator shows +30%, the price is "overheated" and may soon return to the attractor.

mechanism: CNeuronSkillsEncoder: each univariate channel is an agent; CATCH frequency-domain masked cross-observation attention enriches local series with shared market patterns without full centralization; transpose→two conv layers emit per-agent skill SoftMax vectors; contrastive DiversityLoss separates skills across agents and across consecutive timesteps (prev skills concatenated). Common vs task-specific skills planned hierarchically (this part builds encoder only).
data_needed: Multimodal HistoryBars×variables; CATCH time_step/window/heads; skills count; DiversityLoss on 2×heads skill concat.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Single-instrument multimodal bar features as multi-agent univariate sequences; continuation article for full test TBD.
why_new_for_mis: Per-channel hierarchical skill probabilities with frequency-domain cross-enrichment and temporal contrastive diversity give MIS a multi-factor regime embedding (which skills dominate now vs prior bar).
quote: information exchange does not occur directly, but through a masked attention mechanism.... high-frequency components typically reflect short-term volatility and noise, while low-frequency components capture trends and long-term patterns.
